A also pairs the smaller face (advance 12.92 CSS px) with the looser pitch (38 CSS px, ratio 1.77) while B pairs the larger face (13.12) with 37px at 1.69 — a bigger size cannot take a smaller pitch on a one-pitch-per-step ladder, so A's pair is the one that misses its step. states.name: quattro
states.gap: A's syntax markers are #7A7A7A (~4.1:1 on #F9F9F9) against B's #9E9E9E (~2.6:1) — one greyscale step louder, so the `**` bracketing "bottle" and the `*…*` around the italic clause carry visible ink inside the sentence instead of ghosting behind it; A also sets 74px pitch (37 CSS) against B's 76px (38 CSS) at identical cap height, i.e. ~1.76 vs ~1.81, the denser of the two.
states.gapTheirs: B breaks the flush left edge four ways: body text at x=622, h1 text at 667, h2 text at 691, list text at 667 (device px; 22–35 CSS px of drift) because the `#`, `##` and `-` sit in the flow at x=621–627 instead of hanging. A holds every text edge at x=623 and hangs the markers out to 570 / 546 / 576. B also uses two different greys for the same class of mark — #9E9E9E for `#`/`##`/`*`/`**` but #7A7A7A for the list dash.
states.verdict: Both are on a clean grid — A locks to 74px, B to 76px, blank lines are exactly 2× pitch in both, headings get the same air above and below — so this comes down to the left edge, and B's is a staircase: your eye starts a paragraph at one x, a heading 45px right of it, an H2 69px right of it. A hangs the hashes and dashes into the margin and gives you one edge to write down, which is the whole point of the gutter. A pays for it with markers a step too dark — the `**` around "bottle" reads as content — but a noisy asterisk is a smaller tax than a column that won't stand still.
secondary: Type size identical: cap height 30 device px, ascender-to-descender 41 px, both images
Pitch differs 74 vs 76 device px at identical size, so one of the two misses its own ladder step; the pixels don't say which
A is ~2% looser tracked: 22.97 vs 22.53 device px per character over the same 66-advance run — 69 vs 71 characters on line 1
Measure is effectively equal: A body 623→2245 max, B 622→2255 max
Caret identical in both: 6 device px (3 CSS) wide, height exactly one line pitch (74 / 76), same cyan
Bold renders as a true bold weight and the italic clause as true italic in both — no synthesised slant either side
Both keep list items at plain pitch with no extra gap between bullets

states.name: mono
states.gap: Body ink is #1c1c1c on a #f9f9f9 field — 15.3:1, essentially maximum black on 98% white, where B's #cdcdcc on #1a1b1a sits at 11.0:1. It is a glare slab for a four-hour drafting session; the ink wants softening toward ~#2e2e2e, and A's grey markers land at 3.90:1, just under the 4.5:1 AA floor.
states.gapTheirs: Markup markers are rendered at exactly the body ink value — the `#` and both `*` sample #cdcdcc, byte-identical to the prose #cdcdcc (0 delta), and the `#` is bold along with the heading. A demotes the same markers to #7a7a7a against #1c1c1c text, roughly 55% of the text's luminance contrast (3.9:1 vs 15.3:1).
states.verdict: In B the title reads as a title that literally starts with a hash, and the line reads 'time. *Nothing out there is ever in a hurry,* her father' with two live asterisks sitting in the sentence at full prose weight — the syntax is competing with the writing instead of getting out of its way, which is the one job a markdown type stack has. A greys the same markers to #7a7a7a so the `#` falls back into the margin and the asterisks bracket the italic without joining it. B compounds it with a fractional line pitch: baselines at 194/268/341/414/487 give 74/73/73/73px against A's exact 74/74/74/74, so the column drifts a pixel a line and the rhythm never quite locks. And B's ink mass runs 7.3% heavier per em than A's despite a 1.6% smaller advance (25.02 vs 25.41px) — light-on-dark bloom left uncompensated, when dark mode needs the weight taken down, not up.
secondary: Both crops 1760x520; identical typeface, hanging markers at x=10, text left edge x=63 (A) / x=62 (B)
Advance per char: A 25.41px vs B 25.02px — B ~1.6% smaller at the same viewport, fitting ~64 ch/line vs A's ~62

Blank line before body is exactly 2 pitches in both (A 147.5px, B 146px) — neither wastes or shortchanges the gap
A's glyph bands measure 33px tall vs B's 31px; B's stems render visibly softer/blurrier at 4x zoom, A's snap cleanly
B's background #1a1b1a carries a faint green cast (max chroma 0.78%); A is perfectly neutral (chroma 0)
